name: Siegestor
elevationDatum: Rigid local foundation y=0; real metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Two mapped controls fix rotation, baked into the geometry once. No terrain or Mercator stretch.
note: Siegestor with three open barrel-vaulted passages, eight classical facade columns, a tall attic, four stone figures and Bavaria’s four-lion quadriga on the crown. The often-quoted 21 m height is not explicit about the quadriga; it is treated here as the masonry body, with 26 m total an estimated sculpture-inclusive height. This interpretation and the crown proportions need independent dimensional review. Arch radii, column capitals and sculpture poses are original low-detail estimates. Modern north/south facade differences are simplified; inscriptions, lettering and narrative relief panels are omitted. Cityscape: not tested; Full 3D world: not tested. Review follow-up: Lower ellipsoid, limb, arch, wreath and column segmentation removes disproportionate detail; tiny elbow/hand joint balls are omitted while all draped torsos, bent arms, heads, lion bodies, manes, muzzles, legs and paws remain. Sampling compensation keeps the original sculpture extents. Three through-passages and curved soffits, four separate lions, standing Bavaria and 26 m total height survive both LODs. Tests enforce the 5000/2000 total caps and 2000 near bronze cap; the new sheet confirms the same principal silhouette.
